events.title: Heraclius is crowned Byzantine emperor
events.description: Having reached Constantinople on 3 October at the head of the revolt against the unpopular emperor Phocas, Heraclius was crowned in the Chapel of St Stephen within the Great Palace. He reigned until 641.
events.html: Having reached Constantinople on 3 October at the head of the revolt against the unpopular emperor Phocas, Heraclius was crowned in the Chapel of St Stephen within the Great Palace. He reigned until 641.

events.title: Pope Stephen IV crowns Louis the Pious emperor at Reims
events.description: Louis the Pious, co-emperor with his father Charlemagne since 813 and sole ruler of the Franks since 814, received an imperial coronation from Pope Stephen IV at Reims. The next year he settled his succession in the Ordinatio imperii.
events.html: Louis the Pious, co-emperor with his father Charlemagne since 813 and sole ruler of the Franks since 814, received an imperial coronation from Pope Stephen IV at Reims. The next year he settled his succession in the Ordinatio imperii.

events.title: The Fourth Council of Constantinople opens
events.description: A church council opened in Constantinople that deposed the patriarch Photius. Counted by the Catholic Church as the eighth ecumenical council but rejected by the Orthodox, it foreshadowed the later schism between East and West.

events.title: Alfonso VII recognises Afonso Henriques as king of Portugal
events.description: In the Treaty of Zamora, Alfonso VII of León and Castile acknowledged his cousin Afonso Henriques as king of Portugal, in the presence of the papal legate. The treaty is regarded as the founding act of the Kingdom of Portugal.

events.title: Gluck's Orfeo ed Euridice premieres in Vienna
events.description: Christoph Willibald Gluck's Orfeo ed Euridice was first performed at the Burgtheater in Vienna. Its simplicity and dramatic directness began Gluck's reform of opera away from showy vocal display.
events.html: Christoph Willibald Gluck's Orfeo ed Euridice was first performed at the Burgtheater in Vienna. Its simplicity and dramatic directness began Gluck's reform of opera away from showy vocal display.

events.title: Parisian women march on Versailles
events.description: Thousands of Parisians, led by market women angry at the price of bread, marched to Versailles. The next day they brought Louis XVI and his family back to Paris, placing the monarchy under the eye of the Revolution.

events.title: Dr. No premieres, launching the James Bond films
events.description: Dr. No, starring Sean Connery as Ian Fleming's secret agent, premiered at the London Pavilion. It began one of the longest-running series in cinema history.

events.title: The Beatles release their first single, 'Love Me Do'
events.description: Parlophone released 'Love Me Do', the Beatles' debut single in Britain. It reached only number 17, but within a year the band from Liverpool had become a national sensation.
